beats.text: You filmed the whole concert. Now try to remember it.
In a museum study, students looked at some objects and photographed others.
The next day, they remembered the photographed ones worse.
Psychologists call it the photo-taking impairment effect.
One idea: your brain hands the job to the camera. It's saved, so why remember?
But zooming in on one detail helped people remember the whole object.
So take the photo. Then look up, and actually look.

sources: Henkel (2014). Point-and-shoot memories: The influence of taking photos on memory for a museum tour. Psychological Science 25(2). Exp 1: 28 students, 15 objects observed / 15 photographed; photographed objects remembered worse next day. Exp 2: 46 students; zooming in on a detail preserved memory for the whole object. Via Live Science.
